# Accessibility Design Review **VERDICT: REVISE** **Overall Assessment**: The component demonstrates commendable baseline accessibility practices—individual form controls feature programmatic label associations (`htmlFor`), dynamic `aria-invalid` toggling, and contextual `aria-describedby` linking to inline field errors. However, severe design flaws in **focus management** (immediate focus loss to `document.body` caused by disabling the "Next" button upon validation error), **hidden tab stops** (inactive steps rendered off-screen with CSS clip rect and `aria-hidden="true"` while retaining focusable inputs in the DOM), and **missing step state communication** (`aria-current="step"`) undermine operability for keyboard and screen reader users. --- ### Pre-commitment Predictions Before inspecting the source implementation, multi-step wizards with client-side validation typically exhibit: 1. **Focus drops or traps during step transitions and validation failure** (e.g. focus resetting to ``, or focus staying at the bottom of the form after moving to a new step). 2. **Hidden panel focus leakage** (inactive steps visually hidden using `.sr-only` / `clip: rect(...)` techniques or `aria-hidden="true"` without removing child inputs from the Tab order). 3. **Disabled submission/progression buttons** that trap keyboard users or prevent screen reader users from discovering why the form cannot proceed. 4. **Step progress indicators lacking programmatic semantics** (no `aria-current="step"`, no list structure). 5. **Live region timing anomalies and error summary disconnections** (error summary present in live region but disconnected from interactive focus or lacking in-page jump links). *Comparison to Actual Findings:* All five predictions were confirmed in the codebase. --- ### Phase 0: Test Evidence Baseline - **Available Automated Evidence**: None provided. - **Baseline Observation**: While basic automated linters (e.g. standard axe-core runs) might pass label-presence and `aria-describedby` resolution checks, an automated crawl will flag `aria-hidden-focus` on inactive panels, and real keyboard navigation encounters severe focus disorientation. --- ### Perspective Alarm Levels | Perspective | Alarm Level | Trigger Signal | |-------------|-------------|----------------| | **Screen reader** | **HIGH** | Inactive inputs inside `aria-hidden="true"` containers; missing `aria-current="step"`; focus loss to body on validation failure. | | **Keyboard-only** | **HIGH** | Tab stops land on invisible inputs in inactive step panels; Next button disables instantly on click, dropping focus to ``. | | **Low vision** | **HIGH** | Inactive step indicator text contrast is 2.46:1 (fails WCAG 1.4.3); `outline: none` on inputs causes invisible focus in Forced Colors Mode. | | **Cognitive** | **MEDIUM** | Missing `autocomplete` attributes on personal data fields; error summary lacks direct jump links to invalid inputs. | | **Vestibular & motion** | **LOW** | No motion, animations, or transitions present. | | **Auditory access** | **LOW** | No audio or video media present. | | **Environmental contrast** | **HIGH** | Text contrast on inactive steps (`#94a3b8` on `#f8fafc`) fails 4.5:1 minimum; focus outline invisible in Windows High Contrast Mode. | --- ## Critical Findings (Blocks Access) ### 1. Inactive Step Panels Contain Focusable Elements Inside `aria-hidden="true"` - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:53-54, 71-72` and `MultiStepForm.css:49-56` - **Elements Involved**: `
` containing `` elements (`#street`, `#zip` on step 0; `#name`, `#email` on step 1). - **Impacted Users**: Keyboard-only users and screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver). - **WCAG / APG Citation**: **WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A)**, **WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A)**, **WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)**; axe rule `aria-hidden-focus`. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: In `.step-hidden`, the CSS uses `position: absolute; clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0); width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden;`. This technique visually clips content but does **not** remove descendants from the tab sequence (unlike `display: none`, `visibility: hidden`, or the `inert` attribute). Consequently: 1. A keyboard user tabbing through Step 0 will tab directly from `#email` into `#street` and `#zip`—which are completely invisible on screen. Sighted keyboard users' focus indicator disappears into thin air. 2. Because the parent container has `aria-hidden="true"`, screen readers will either announce nothing when focus lands on these inputs or behave erratically (focusing an element the accessibility tree was told does not exist). - **Fix**: Apply `hidden` or `display: none` to inactive panels, or use the HTML `inert` attribute (`inert={step !== 0}`) so that inactive step inputs are completely removed from both visual layout and the accessibility/tab tree. ``` ### A11y Evidence Finding finding_id: hidden_panel_retains_tab_stops fingerprint: a7f89c42b10e39d4 source: MultiStepForm.jsx:53-54, 71-72 & MultiStepForm.css:49-56 wcag_or_apg: WCAG 2.1.1, WCAG 4.1.2, axe-core:aria-hidden-focus section_508_fpc_context: WCAG 2.0 2.1.1 (Keyboard), 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) severity: CRITICAL perspective_alarms: screen_reader=HIGH, keyboard_only=HIGH evidence: MultiStepForm.jsx:53 `
` with MultiStepForm.css:49 `.step-hidden { position: absolute; clip: rect(0,0,0,0); }` reproduction_steps: 1. Render form at step 0. 2. Focus #email. 3. Press Tab. 4. Observe focus moves to invisible #street inside aria-hidden div. expected_behavior: Inactive form panels and their focusable inputs must be excluded from the keyboard tab sequence. actual_behavior: Inactive panel inputs remain fully focusable via Tab, causing focus to enter an aria-hidden off-screen node. trend: new ``` --- ### 2. "Next" Button Disables Immediately on Validation Error, Causing Instant Focus Loss to `document.body` - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:104` (``) - **Elements Involved**: `` reproduction_steps: 1. Leave form fields empty on Step 0. 2. Focus "Next" button with keyboard. 3. Press Enter or Space. 4. Inspect document.activeElement. expected_behavior: Focus remains within the form context and moves to the first invalid field (#name) or the error summary container. actual_behavior: Button disables dynamically; browser drops focus to document.body. trend: new ``` --- ## Major Findings (Significantly Degrades Experience) ### 3. Step Progression Indicator Lacks `aria-current="step"` and Semantic Ordered List Structure - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:38-45` - **Elements Involved**: `
` containing `` elements. - **Impacted Users**: Screen reader users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: **WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A)**, **WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)**. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: The active step is conveyed visually by `.active` CSS styling (`color: #1e40af; background: #dbeafe`), but programmatically there is no `aria-current="step"` on the active step. A screen reader user navigating through the indicator hears "Personal Info (1 of 3)", "Address (2 of 3)", etc., but cannot distinguish which step is currently active. Furthermore, step indicators represent a sequential ordered workflow, which should be structured as an `
    ` rather than unstructured `` elements inside a generic `role="group"`. - **Fix**: Use an `
      ` with `
    1. ` elements, and place `aria-current="step"` on the active step item. --- ### 4. Absence of Focus Management on Step Transition (Stranded Focus) - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:33` (`const next = () => { if (validate()) setStep(s => Math.min(s + 1, 2)); };`) - **Elements Involved**: Wizard step state transition logic. - **Impacted Users**: Screen reader and keyboard users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: **WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order (Level A)**. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: When the user successfully advances from Step 0 to Step 1, the new step's fields and heading render above the "Next" / "Back" buttons. However, focus remains on the "Next" button at the bottom of the form. The user is given no indication that Step 1 has loaded, and pressing Tab moves focus out of the form or to the Back button. Keyboard and screen reader users are forced to manually reverse-tab up through the new fields to discover them. - **Fix**: When `step` increments, programmatically set focus to the new step's heading (e.g. `

      `) or to the first input of the new step. --- ### 5. Inactive Step Dot Color Contrast Fails Minimum Threshold (2.46:1) - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.css:20, 23` - **Elements Involved**: `.step-dot` (`color: #94a3b8; background: #f8fafc;`) - **Impacted Users**: Low vision users and users under outdoor/glare conditions. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: **WCAG 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA)**. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: Text size for `.step-dot` is `13px` (below the `18pt` / `14pt bold` large text threshold). The calculated contrast ratio between `#94a3b8` and `#f8fafc` is **2.46:1**, falling far short of the required **4.5:1** minimum contrast for body text. Inactive steps are nearly illegible for users with low vision. - **Fix**: Change `.step-dot` color to `#64748b` or darker on `#f8fafc` (which yields a contrast ratio of 4.7:1). --- ### 6. Focus Outline Suppressed Without High Contrast Mode Alternative - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.css:79-83` - **Elements Involved**: `.field-group input:focus` (`outline: none; border-color: #3b82f6; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.15);`) - **Impacted Users**: Low vision, keyboard-only, and Windows High Contrast (Forced Colors) Mode users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: **WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA)**, **WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (Level AAA / Best Practice)**. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: 1. `box-shadow` is stripped out entirely by Windows High Contrast Mode / Forced Colors Mode. Because `outline: none` is set, inputs show **zero focus indication** in High Contrast Mode. 2. The box shadow opacity is extremely faint (`rgba(..., 0.15)`), and the border change from `#cbd5e1` to `#3b82f6` does not achieve the required 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors. - **Fix**: Preserve an explicit outline (e.g. `outline: 2px solid #3b82f6; outline-offset: 2px;` or `outline: 2px solid transparent;` for forced-colors fallbacks). --- ### 7. Error Summary Lacks Direct Navigation Links and Unused `liveRef` - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:46-51` - **Elements Involved**: `
      ` - **Impacted Users**: Screen reader, keyboard-only, and cognitive accessibility users. - **WCAG / APG Citation**: **WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification (Level A)**, **WCAG 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (Level AA)**, WAI-ARIA APG Form Validation pattern. - **Confidence**: HIGH - **Why this matters**: 1. The component creates `const liveRef = useRef(null);` and attaches it, but **never references or focuses it**. 2. When validation fails, errors appear in a `
        `, but items are static text (`
      • {msg}
        • `) rather than in-page jump links (`...`). Keyboard and screen reader users cannot quickly jump from the error summary directly to the invalid input. 3. Notice also the April 2026 Audit Check: inline errors already use `aria-describedby`, which is correct. But the error summary region is unlinked to navigation and announces re-renders on keystroke clearing without focusing the first error. - **Fix**: Convert error summary list items into anchor links pointing to field IDs (`{msg}`). When validation fails, focus the error summary container (`tabIndex={-1}`). --- ## Minor Findings (Friction But Workaround Exists) 1. **Missing `autocomplete` attributes on Personal Data Inputs** - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:58, 65, 76, 83` - **WCAG Citation**: **WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (Level AA)** - **Details**: Personal information fields (name, email, street address, zip code) lack HTML `autoComplete` tokens (`name`, `email`, `street-address`, `postal-code`). This prevents browser autofill and password/form managers from aiding users with cognitive or motor impairments. 2. **Missing Grouping Semantics (`
        ` and ``)** - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:53, 71` - **WCAG Citation**: **WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A)** - **Details**: Step panels use plain `
        ` containers with `

        ` headings. Grouping controls inside `
        ` with `` provides built-in context announcements for screen readers when navigating between fields. 3. **CSS Class Mismatch for Completed Step Indicator** - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:41` vs `MultiStepForm.css:32` - **WCAG Citation**: **WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)** - **Details**: In JSX, completed steps receive `${i < step ? 'done' : ''}`, but the CSS rule is named `.step-dot.completed`. As a result, completed steps never receive visual completed styling, nor do they communicate completion status to assistive technology. 4. **ZIP Code Format Constraint Only Announced After Failure** - **Location**: `MultiStepForm.jsx:82-86` - **WCAG Citation**: **WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A)** - **Details**: The 5-digit format requirement for the ZIP code is not communicated in advance via a hint text (`aria-describedby`). Users only discover the constraint after triggering validation failure. --- ## Enhancements (Best Practice Not Met) 1. **Top-Level Page Landmark & Document Heading**: The form lacks a parent `
        ` landmark and a top-level `

        ` naming the workflow (e.g. `

        Registration Wizard

        `), which leaves heading navigation starting at `

        `. 2. **Review Step Direct Edit Affordances**: On Step 2 (Confirm), the summary definition list `
        ` provides no "Edit" links or shortcuts back to Step 0 or Step 1. If a user spots a typo in their name on Step 2, they must activate "Back" twice to correct it. 3. **Step Clearing Announcement**: When an error is resolved in `update()`, the error disappears from `errors` state, but there is no polite announcement confirming that the field's error was resolved. --- ## What's Missing (Gaps & Unhandled Edge Cases) - **Missing programmatic focus shift on validation failure**: Focus is not redirected to the error list or first invalid field. - **Missing programmatic focus shift on step transition**: Focus remains on the bottom action button when steps change. - **Missing `inert` or `hidden` on inactive panels**: Inactive panels remain in the accessibility tree and keyboard sequence. - **Missing `aria-current="step"` on active step indicator**: Current position is communicated visually only. - **Missing jump links (``) in error summary**: Error items cannot be activated to navigate to fields. - **Missing `autocomplete` attributes**: Fields fail WCAG 1.3.5. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user (NVDA / VoiceOver)**: Screen reader users will experience multiple severe disruptions. On validation failure, focus is unexpectedly dropped to ``. On step transition, focus remains stranded at the bottom of the page with no announcement that Step 1 has loaded. Inactive step inputs can be focused even though their container is marked `aria-hidden="true"`, causing silent or confusing phantom focus stops. - **Keyboard-only user**: Tabbing through the form lands on invisible inputs in hidden step panels because `.step-hidden` does not use `display: none`. Furthermore, when Next is pressed and validation fails, the button disables immediately, throwing focus back to the top of the browser window. - **Low vision user**: Inactive step indicators have a contrast ratio of only 2.46:1, making the workflow sequence almost unreadable. Input focus indicators rely on faint `box-shadow` and have no explicit outline, making them completely invisible in Windows High Contrast Mode. - **Cognitive accessibility user**: Fields collecting personal data lack `autocomplete` assistance. When validation fails, the user is not automatically directed to the problem fields, and the error summary does not provide clickable links to jump to errors. --- ## Realist Check & Severity Calibration 1. *Inactive inputs focusable in clip rect:* Realistic worst case is keyboard users getting stuck in invisible form fields while screen readers emit conflicting states. This is a severe disruption affecting all keyboard and AT users. **Confirmed CRITICAL**. 2. *Next button disabled on error:* Clicking Next with empty fields immediately drops focus to `document.body`. Users must navigate through the entire page from scratch to get back to the form. **Confirmed CRITICAL**. 3. *Missing `aria-current="step"` and step transition focus:* Degrades comprehension of where the user is in the wizard. **Confirmed MAJOR**. 4. *Step indicator contrast (2.46:1):* Directly violates WCAG 1.4.3 Level AA on standard screens. **Confirmed MAJOR**. --- ## Verdict Justification **VERDICT: REVISE** While the author successfully implemented basic inline labeling and `aria-describedby` associations, the form contains two access-blocking **CRITICAL** issues: 1. Focusable `` elements remain inside clipped, `aria-hidden="true"` containers. 2. The progression button dynamically disables upon validation error, causing the browser to dump focus to `document.body`. Before this component can ship, these two critical issues and the major focus/state management defects (lack of `aria-current="step"`, lack of transition focus management, and suppressed focus outlines) must be corrected. --- ## Actionable Remediation Code ### 1. Updated Component Logic (`MultiStepForm.jsx`) ```jsx import React, { useState, useRef } from 'react'; const STEPS = ['Personal Info', 'Address', 'Confirm']; const MultiStepForm = () => { const [step, setStep] = useState(0); const [data, setData] = useState({ name: '', email: '', street: '', zip: '' }); const [errors, setErrors] = useState({}); const errorSummaryRef = useRef(null); const stepHeadingRef = useRef(null); const update = (e) => { const { name, value } = e.target; setData(prev => ({ ...prev, [name]: value })); if (errors[name]) { const next = { ...errors }; delete next[name]; setErrors(next); } }; const validate = () => { const errs = {}; if (step === 0) { if (!data.name.trim()) errs.name = 'Full name is required.'; if (!data.email.includes('@')) errs.email = 'Enter a valid email address.'; } else if (step === 1) { if (!data.street.trim()) errs.street = 'Street address is required.'; if (!/^\d{5}$/.test(data.zip)) errs.zip = 'ZIP code must be 5 digits.'; } setErrors(errs); if (Object.keys(errs).length > 0) { // Focus error summary or first invalid field setTimeout(() => { if (errorSummaryRef.current) { errorSummaryRef.current.focus(); } }, 0); return false; } return true; }; const next = () => { if (validate()) { setStep(s => { const nextStep = Math.min(s + 1, 2); setTimeout(() => stepHeadingRef.current?.focus(), 0); return nextStep; }); } }; const back = () => { setErrors({}); setStep(s => { const prevStep = Math.max(s - 1, 0); setTimeout(() => stepHeadingRef.current?.focus(), 0); return prevStep; }); }; const hasErrors = Object.keys(errors).length > 0; return (
        e.preventDefault()} className="wizard-form" noValidate> {/* Ordered List for Step Navigation */}
          {STEPS.map((label, i) => (
        1. Step {i + 1}: {label} ({i + 1} of {STEPS.length})
          2. ))}
        {/* Accessible Error Summary */}
        {hasErrors && (

        Please correct the following errors:

          {Object.entries(errors).map(([k, msg]) => (
        • {msg}
          • ))}
        )}
        {/* Step 0 - Personal Information */}

        Personal Information

        {errors.name && {errors.name}}
        {errors.email && {errors.email}}
        {/* Step 1 - Address */}

        Address

        {errors.street && {errors.street}}
        5-digit postal code (e.g., 90210) {errors.zip && {errors.zip}}
        {/* Step 2 - Confirmation */} {step === 2 && (

        Confirm Your Information

        Name
        {data.name}
        Email
        {data.email}
        Address
        {data.street}, {data.zip}
        )} {/* Actions (Never use disabled={hasErrors} on Next) */}
        {step > 0 && ( )} {step < 2 ? ( ) : ( )}
        ); }; export default MultiStepForm; ``` ### 2. Updated CSS Improvements (`MultiStepForm.css`) ```css /* Accessible list styling for progress */ .step-indicator { display: flex; list-style: none; padding: 0 0 16px 0; margin: 0 0 24px 0; justify-content: space-between; border-bottom: 1px solid #e2e8f0; } /* Inactive text contrast fixed to >= 4.5:1 (#64748b on #f8fafc = 4.7:1) */ .step-dot { font-size: 13px; color: #475569; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: 16px; background: #f8fafc; } .step-dot.active { color: #1e40af; background: #dbeafe; font-weight: 600; } .step-dot.completed { color: #065f46; background: #d1fae5; } /* Ensure focus outline is visible in all modes, including Windows High Contrast */ .field-group input:focus { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: 2px; border-color: #2563eb; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(37, 99, 235, 0.2); } .error-region:focus { outline: 2px solid #dc2626; outline-offset: 4px; } .field-hint { display: block; font-size: 12px; color: #64748b; margin-bottom: 4px; } .error-list a { color: #991b1b; text-decoration: underline; font-weight: 600; } .error-list a:focus { outline: 2px solid #991b1b; outline-offset: 2px; } ``` --- ## Open Questions (Unscored) 1. **Destructive Action Handling on Back Navigation**: Activating `back()` immediately executes `setErrors({})` and leaves input state preserved, but should previously validated field errors be retained or re-validated when navigating forward again? 2. **Server-Side Validation Feedback**: If submission on Step 2 encounters backend verification errors, where will server errors be injected, and will they reuse the polite summary region?
